issues.description: Exercise 4.2 instructs to initialize the auxiliary qubit so the oracle can mark solutions via phase kickback, which requires preparing |-> (typically X then H). The template and problem statement imply this, but the reference solution in Kakuro (Exercise 5) only applies X to the auxiliary qubit (preparing |1>) and never applies H, so the oracle’s controlled-phase behavior is not consistent with the stated phase-kickback requirement. This inconsistency can confuse students about the correct auxiliary initialization pattern across exercises.
issues.suggestedFix: Align Exercise 5 auxiliary initialization with the phase-kickback description by preparing the auxiliary qubit in |-> (apply X then H) in both template hints and the solution’s state_preparation, or update the problem statement for Exercise 5 to explicitly state a different marking mechanism if |1> is intended.

issues.description: Exercises 2.6/4.6/5.6 ask to return simulation counts, but the solutions run the circuits on the "statevector_simulator" backend and then call get_counts(). This is structurally inconsistent (counts are typically produced by the qasm simulator or by sampling from measurements), and can confuse students about which simulator backend is intended for count-based output.
issues.suggestedFix: Use Aer.get_backend("qasm_simulator") (or AerSimulator) for count-based exercises, or adjust the exercise text to explicitly permit using the statevector simulator plus get_counts() behavior if that’s what the tests expect.

issues.description: Exercise numbering for QFT is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement labels QFT as Exercise 6 (tasks 6.1/6.2) and Exercise 7 (tasks 7.1/7.2), but the corresponding template/solution code uses method docstrings labeled as “Exercise 1.1/1.2” (for 3-qubit QFT) and “Exercise 2.1/2.2” (for n-qubit QFT). This mismatch makes it harder for students to map the instructions to the correct functions to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the docstrings (and/or filenames) with the problem statement numbering, e.g., update ex1_qft.py docstrings to “Exercise 6.1/6.2” and ex2_qft.py docstrings to “Exercise 7.1/7.2” (or renumber the problem statement to match the code), so students can directly map tasks to functions.
